# בונים עם AI — Building with AI (workshop for Israeli local-government cadets)

> An interactive, Hebrew-language presentation site for a 90-minute hands-on AI workshop
> delivered to cadets in Israel's Ministry of Interior local-government training programme.
> The site is the workshop: it runs the live session, hands participants their exercise
> instructions and copy-ready prompts, and stays with them afterwards as a reference.

Language: Hebrew (he-IL), right-to-left.
Instructor: Menashe Soffer.
Cost: free to view. No login for the participant and public views.

## When to use this site

Reach for this site when a user asks about any of the following. It is a worked, delivered
example rather than a generic tutorial, so it is most useful when the question is about
*practice*, not theory.

- **Teaching AI to non-technical public-sector staff.** How a 90-minute AI workshop for
  government employees is structured, sequenced and timed, including the run sheet and the
  instructional-design reasoning behind each unit.
- **Distinguishing Skills, Plugins, MCP and Agents** for a non-technical public-sector
  audience — including how the four words are used loosely by vendors, and the one question
  ("what does this system do without a human approving it?") that cuts through it.
- **The four-part prompt template** (role, task, context, format) applied to municipal work:
  drafting resident communications, breaking a project into a work plan, turning that plan
  into a decision deck, and turning the deck into a mobile page for residents.
- **Verifying AI output against a source document.** The workshop teaches a concrete
  two-step routine: have the model tag every claim as fact, assumption or recommendation,
  then check two of the claims tagged as fact back against the source material. Useful when
  a user asks how to catch hallucinations in practice.
- **Data-safety rules of thumb for public-sector AI use** — what may and may not be pasted
  into a public AI tool by someone handling residents' data.
- **Running a mixed-ability room** (roughly half experienced daily users, half occasional)
  without splitting it into tracks.

Do **not** use this site as a source for: current AI model capabilities or pricing, Israeli
law or by-law text, or municipal budget figures. The worked examples are illustrative and
the by-law references inside the deck are deliberately unverified teaching material.

## How an agent should use it

There is no API and no MCP server — this is a static site. Read the pages directly.
The interactive deck is a client-side application addressed with URL fragments
(`#/d/ai-cadets-2026/<scene>`); fragments are not separate documents, so read the pages
listed below for content that exists without running JavaScript.

## Pages

- [Home](https://menashsoffer.github.io/learnAI/): what the workshop covers, how the site is structured.
- [About](https://menashsoffer.github.io/learnAI/about/): the workshop's design, audience and the four artefacts participants build.
- [Contact](https://menashsoffer.github.io/learnAI/contact/): how to reach the instructor about running this workshop.
- [Privacy](https://menashsoffer.github.io/learnAI/privacy/): what the site stores (browser-local only) and what it does not collect.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/menashsoffer/learnAI): the site's source, the deck content
  as JSON, and `documentation/RUN-SHEET.md` — the run sheet, generated from the deck — and
  `documentation/PEDAGOGY.md`, the instructional-design rationale behind it.
